findings.title: Unsanitized raw HTML from imported content rendered directly in embed view
findings.body: Posts imported via TopicEmbed.import use cook_method raw_html (see app/models/post.rb Post#cook), which causes Post#cook to simply `return raw` and skip PrettyText's sanitization pipeline entirely. That raw content (scraped via Readability from arbitrary remote URLs, or pulled from an RSS/Atom feed) is then rendered unescaped here with `raw post.cooked`. Any script tags or event handlers present in the source page/feed will execute inside the embed iframe (and via postMessage/window.parent access can potentially reach the embedding site). Since the content source is an external, non-Discourse-controlled URL/feed, this is a stored XSS vector that bypasses the normal content-safety pipeline used for all other posts.

findings.title: postMessage origin check uses substring match instead of exact comparison
findings.body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` rejects a message only if `e.origin` cannot be found anywhere inside `discourseUrl`. Because `indexOf` performs a substring search rather than an origin equality check, an attacker-controlled origin that is merely a prefix/substring of the real discourseUrl (e.g. `http://example.co` when discourseUrl is `http://example.com/`) will pass this check and be allowed to send `discourse-resize` messages that control the iframe's height, defeating the intended origin restriction.

findings.title: Access control relies solely on the client-supplied Referer header
findings.body: `ensure_embeddable` authorizes embedding purely by comparing `request.referer`'s host to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. The Referer header is fully attacker-controlled on non-browser requests (curl, scripts, server-to-server calls), so this check can be trivially bypassed to call `/embed/best`, triggering TopicEmbed/TopicRetriever logic (including outbound HTTP fetches) for arbitrary allowed hosts without ever being embedded on the real site. It also doesn't verify scheme, so http and https referers are treated identically.

findings.title: X-Frame-Options value 'ALLOWALL' is not a standard directive
findings.body: The X-Frame-Options header only defines DENY, SAMEORIGIN and ALLOW-FROM <uri> as valid values. 'ALLOWALL' is not part of the spec; some browsers may ignore the unrecognized value (making the header a no-op) while others could treat it conservatively and block framing, which would silently break the embed feature for some users/browsers. Omitting the header (the real intent here) would be the correct way to allow framing by any origin.

findings.title: Outbound fetch of user-controlled embed_url has no scheme/SSRF restriction
findings.body: `import_remote` calls `open(url).read` (Kernel#open from open-uri) on a URL that ultimately originates from the public, unauthenticated `embed_url` query parameter in EmbedController#best. The only restriction applied upstream (TopicRetriever#invalid_host?) checks that the URI's host matches SiteSetting.embeddable_host, but the scheme, port, and full path are attacker-controlled. This allows triggering server-side requests to arbitrary ports/paths on the configured host (SSRF), and relies on the Kernel#open/open-uri pattern which is also known to execute shell commands if the string begins with a pipe character — a defense-in-depth concern given this value flows from request params through two layers before reaching open().

findings.title: Unhandled race condition on unique embed_url constraint
findings.body: `TopicEmbed.import` checks `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and only creates a new TopicEmbed via `create!` if none exists. There's a unique index on embed_url (see db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb), but the check-then-create is not atomic. Two concurrent imports for the same URL (e.g. the hourly PollFeed job and a user-triggered RetrieveTopic job, which can itself invoke PollFeed synchronously — see lib/topic_retriever.rb) can both see `embed.blank?` as true and both attempt `TopicEmbed.create!`, causing one to raise an unhandled ActiveRecord error (RecordNotUnique/RecordInvalid) and crash the job instead of gracefully falling back to the update path.

findings.title: TopicEmbed.import mutates the caller-supplied contents argument
findings.body: `contents << "\n<hr>..."` mutates the string object passed in by the caller via the `<<` operator rather than creating a new string. This is a surprising side effect for callers that reuse the string afterward, and will raise a FrozenStringError if the caller passes a frozen string literal (e.g. under `# frozen_string_literal: true`), which is increasingly common in Ruby codebases.

findings.title: Full feed poll executed synchronously and redundantly on every embed cache miss
findings.body: `perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` directly and synchronously (bypassing Jobs.enqueue) whenever feed polling is enabled and the requested embed isn't found. This means every single unmatched embed request re-fetches and re-processes the *entire* configured RSS/Atom feed inline within the RetrieveTopic job, duplicating the work already done by the hourly scheduled PollFeed job. Under load (many simultaneous first-time embed requests), this can cause repeated, expensive network fetches of the whole feed and increases the window for the race condition described in TopicEmbed.import.

findings.title: poll_feed assumes every feed item has a non-nil content field
findings.body: `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` calls `.scrub` directly on `i.content` without checking for nil. Many RSS 2.0 feeds only populate `description` and not a `content`/`content:encoded` element, so SimpleRSS would return nil for `i.content`, causing a NoMethodError that aborts processing of the entire feed for that run (sidekiq_options retry: false means the job silently fails with no retry).

findings.title: feed_key method is defined but never used
findings.body: `feed_key` builds a Redis key intended to track feed modification state (e.g. for conditional GET / Last-Modified caching), but it is never referenced anywhere in poll_feed.rb or elsewhere in the diff. This looks like an incomplete feature: the feed is always fully fetched and fully re-processed on every hourly run with no change-detection short-circuit, which is wasteful for large feeds and puts unnecessary load on the external feed source.

findings.title: Pre-existing migration modified to add force: true
findings.body: This migration (dated 2013-12-23) already existed prior to this PR and is being edited to add `force: true` to `create_table`. Editing an already-committed migration changes its behavior depending on whether an environment has already run it: environments that ran the old version have a table without the force-drop semantics, while fresh environments running the edited version will drop-and-recreate on every migrate (or fail unexpectedly on table already existing in edge cases). The correct approach is a new migration if the table needs to be recreated, to keep migration history reproducible across all environments.

findings.title: disqus.thor loses category assignment and original thread timestamp without replacement
findings.body: The `--category`/`-c` method_option and the category-resolution logic were removed entirely, and the topic-creation call was switched from `PostCreator.new(user, title:, raw:, created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id)` to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which does not accept a category or created_at. This silently drops two previously supported behaviors (assigning an imported thread to a category, and preserving the original Disqus thread's creation date for the topic's first post) with no replacement, which will surprise existing users of this import task.

findings.title: No test coverage for referer-host mismatch rejection
findings.body: The spec covers 'missing embeddable_host' and 'missing referer' failure cases, but never exercises the actual host-mismatch branch of `ensure_embeddable` (`URI(request.referer).host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`), which is the core security check of the controller. A regression in that comparison (e.g. the substring/case-sensitivity issues noted elsewhere) would not be caught by this test suite.

findings.title: poll_feed's core RSS-processing logic is untested
findings.body: All tests in this file only verify the guard conditions in `execute` (feed_polling_enabled?, feed_polling_url, embed_by_username) and stub out `poll_feed` itself. The actual `poll_feed` method — RSS/Atom parsing via SimpleRSS, URL fallback logic, and the `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` call that can raise on nil content — has no test coverage at all, so bugs such as the nil-content crash noted elsewhere would not be caught.

findings.title: Transient 'loading' placeholder response is cached for 1 minute like the final content
findings.body: `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is applied unconditionally regardless of whether the controller rendered the real topic view or the transient 'loading' placeholder (which itself auto-reloads client-side after 30 seconds, per app/views/embed/loading.html.erb). If this response is cached by any intermediary (browser cache, CDN), the client-side reload after 30s can be served the same stale cached 'loading' page for up to 60 seconds, delaying display of the actual content well past when it became available.
